title: feat(calendar)!: retire the `dateField` / `endField` aliases at both faces (objectui#8355)
body:
Fixes #8355

Director seat, 2026-09-16 (comment `5690901412`), class-1 self-adjudication, option **B extended to the declaration**: 「The two aliases **retire at both faces, now**」. `Clause-②: yes` is declared by the ruling itself.

## The refusal an author writing `dateField` now sees

> ⚠️ **Updated at `c82937e3b`.** The contract review (`5707572631`) returned FAIL on this text and it was right: the message this section first quoted asserted that a calendar carrying either spelling *"never came through the validated path"*, which is false of this package's own `safeValidateSchema`, and it published one consequence for two keys that fail differently. Both are repaired below, and the consequence clause is now **per key**. The block quoted here is dumped from the built mirror, not transcribed.

```text
Unrecognized key(s) on this calendar configuration: `dateField`. Did you mean `dateField` → `startDateField`? `dateField` and `endField` are the pre-#2231 objectui spellings of the calendar date axis, retired at both faces by objectui#8355. `@objectstack/spec` spells the axis `startDateField` and `endDateField` only. ⚠️ This package accepted BOTH legacy spellings green until that retirement — they rode a `.passthrough()` straight through `safeValidateSchema` into `ListView`'s calendar branch, which flattened them onto the generated `object-calendar` node where the renderer's alias ladder read them. That ladder is gone, so the key is refused here instead of being kept and then ignored. Write `startDateField` for the event start. Kept rather than refused, an authored `dateField` binds nothing: the calendar falls through to "Calendar configuration required. Please specify startDateField and titleField.", a screen that names the canonical keys and never the key you wrote.
```

`endField` takes the same stem and a different tail, because the two spellings fail differently — measured on the renderer, not assumed: a calendar that also carries a start binding **still draws**, and only the end of every event is silently dropped.

```text
…Write `endDateField` for the event end. Kept rather than refused, an authored `endField` fails even more quietly than its sibling: a calendar that also carries a start binding still DRAWS, and only the end of every event is silently dropped.
```

On the flat node face the surface noun is `this object-calendar node`. The issue `code` is `invalid_type` at the key's own path on every declared slot, and `custom` at `options.calendar.ALIAS` — two codes, one message per spelling, because an open record can declare no member.

## What shipped — four halves that only work together

> ⚠️ **Updated at `77fbabc6e`.** This section read "three halves" and named `ListView` as the producer. There are **two** producers: the contract review measured that `plugin-view`'s `generateViewSchema` — "the SECOND route to `ObjectCalendar`" in its own comment — still spread the authored block raw, so this PR turned a drawing object-view document into a mute one. That is closed here rather than deferred; see the round-3 note below.

| face | change |
|:--|:--|
| `@object-ui/types` | `aliasKeyRefusal()` arms on the view-level `calendar` block, on the legacy `options.calendar` nesting, on the FLAT `object-calendar` node face, and on that element's own `calendar` container; plus a `.check()` on `ObjectViewSchema` covering a named view's two nestings under `listViews`. Five authoring surfaces. `z.input` of each arm is `undefined`, so the TS face carries `dateField?: never` / `endField?: never` and `tsc` refuses the key at the authoring site too. |
| `@object-ui/plugin-calendar` | `getCalendarConfig` reads the declared spellings only. The `CalendarAliasRungs` cast target, both read sites, and their two entries in the config memo's dependency list are gone. The docblock pointer to this card is rewritten as the ruling requires. |
| `@object-ui/plugin-list` | the `calendar` branch destructures the two spellings out of the merged block and spreads only the remainder onto the node, exactly as the kanban branch strips its own stray `groupBy` (objectui#8365). |
| `@object-ui/plugin-view` | **the second route.** Its calendar branch strips the same two spellings. Measured end to end before any mechanism was chosen: the new pin was written and run against the unmodified head `c82937e3b` and came back **5 red / 6 green**, every control green. |

### Round 3 — the second route, and why `listViews` is still unmirrored

`ObjectViewSchema.listViews` is unmirrored **by ruling**, and that ruling turns on the key's **value type**: neither the spec's strict `ObjectListViewSchema` nor the local `NamedListView` can be the declared value without losing documented behaviour or enforcing 43 unread members, and ⛔ not `z.any()`. A `.check()` on the object decides none of that — it declares no value type, puts no key in `shape`, requires no `columns`, and refuses neither an undeclared key nor the legacy `options` bag. Four pins assert exactly those non-effects, including that `listViews` stays out of `shape` and that the discriminated union still routes an `object-view` and still refuses an unknown discriminator. The in-module precedent is `ListViewSchema.options`, an untyped bag carrying a `.check()` that refuses `kanban.groupBy` and this card's two spellings by name.

⚠️ **A premise died on contact, and it narrows what this check claims.** The read-door silence on that route is **not** this PR's doing and **not** calendar-specific: measured in the same pass, a named view carrying objectui#8365's stray `kanban.groupBy` is **accepted**, while the identical key on a `list-view` document is refused. Every alias refusal this module declares stops at `listViews`. What this PR regressed on the object-view route is the **behaviour** — drew at the merge-base, mute at head — and the check is what makes that loud. It is ⛔ not a general repair of the unmirrored key, and the kanban twin is still silent there.

⛔ **Ladder-without-tombstone is the known-bad state and it is why these are one commit.** The earlier attempt removed the ladder while the producer kept spreading the alias: every calendar block ends `.passthrough()`, so the key was not refused, it was KEPT and then ignored, and the author met a generic "Calendar configuration required" screen naming keys they had not written. The refusal at the declaration is what makes the same document fail loudly.

⛔ **Option A (normalise at the producer) is refused as the end state**, so the aliased view produces **no** date binding at all. A pin on each producer asserts that explicitly — a producer-side fold would emit `startDateField` and every other row in those files would still pass.

⚠️ **The `dateField` consequence clause is now per key AND per surface** (round 3). It named the "Calendar configuration required" screen, which is what happens wherever the value lands as a node **binding** — but not inside the element's own `calendar` container, which `getCalendarConfig` reads **whole**: the calendar mounts and simply places nothing, every record under "Unscheduled". Measured on the renderer across five rows with both controls before the sentence was rewritten. `endField` keeps one clause, because it reads the same on both. That is the second round in a row a consequence string was wrong about a surface it was installed on, so the split is pinned rather than remembered.

## Two declared deviations from the ruling's own wording

1. **`aliasKeyRefusal()` rather than `retirementTombstone()`.** The ruling names the helper `retirementTombstone`. Both live in `packages/types/src/zod/tombstone.zod.ts`, share the same `z.never({ error }).optional().describe()` primitive, the same `invalid_type` code and the same `?: never` TypeScript face; `aliasKeyRefusal` is the family member whose entire purpose is the message the ruling asks for — 「refused by name, text naming `startDateField` / `endDateField`」 — and it is what the structurally identical objectui#8365 arm two consts above uses for `kanban.groupBy`. That file's own vocabulary note reserves `retirementTombstone` for a withdrawing key's migration note and `aliasKeyRefusal` for a sibling spelling. ⇒ the ruled behaviour, in this repo's spelling for it.
2. **The tombstones land on the CALENDAR declarations, not on `TimelineConfig`.** The ruling cites `TimelineConfig` as where objectui declares `dateField`, which is true — it is the only literal `dateField:` member in that file. But a document authoring a calendar alias is validated by `CalendarConfig` / `ObjectCalendarBlockConfigSchema` / `ObjectCalendarSchema`, never by `TimelineConfig`: a tombstone there would refuse nothing this card is about while breaking the timeline lane, which the card's own boundaries put on other cards and which has live consumers (`normalizeListViewSchema` folds `timeline.dateField` onto `startDateField`, `ObjectView` reads it, app-shell pins that it still renders). A pin asserts `timeline.dateField` still parses green, so a later sweep has to say so rather than carrying it in silently.

## Evidence

Every command was run from the repository ROOT. Exit codes were redirected to a file and read back, never through a pipe.

| run | verdict |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build` | exit **0** — `dist completeness: 1 package(s) complete (130 emitted files verified)` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` | exit **0** — `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.examples.json && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`. This is the ONLY gate for the `@ts-expect-error` arms; vitest erases them. |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/ packages/plugin-calendar/ packages/plugin-list/` | **312 files, 5874 tests** — see the note below |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` · `check:changeset-claims` · `check:pending-changeset-literals` · `check:new-line-citations` · `check:test-path-roots` · `check:spec-symbols` | exit **0** each |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` · `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | exit **0** each |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` (9 paths) | exit **0** — `NOT GOVERNED — 9 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched` |

The three-package run first reported `1 failed | 311 passed` on `list-view-spec-parity.test.ts` — its per-view-config ledger enumerates each mirror's local keys, and declaring a refusal is still declaring. That is a ledger repair, not a relaxation: `calendar`'s entry grows to `['defaultView', 'dateField', 'endField']` with the same note the objectui#8365 `groupBy` entry already carries, and a new row asserts the calendar pair is refused while the `timeline.dateField` row one line up stays green. Re-run after the repair: exit **0**, 20 tests.

**Reverse verification, direction predicted before running.** Both new pin files state their own ablation in their header: remove either arm from `CalendarConfig` and the runtime refusal rows go RED while every control stays GREEN and the compile-time arms report TS2578; restore the two raw spreads in `ListView.tsx` and the generated-node rows go RED while every refusal row stays GREEN. Two independent halves, two independent ablations — the asymmetry is what shows neither half is carrying the other.

**Controls carried in every pass** (a narrowing measured only by its subject is a door that refuses everything): the canonical spellings parse green on every surface; an undeclared nonsense key still parses, so no object became strict; the objectui#8365 `options.kanban.groupBy` refusal still fires, because the calendar check was added inside the same `.check()`; and the renderer's refusal screen is shown to be reachable, so a "does not refuse" reading is never vacuous.

## ⚠️ One measured upstream divergence, recorded and NOT fixed here

> ⚠️ **Corrected at `c82937e3b`.** This section, the changeset paragraph and two code comments all called the upstream behaviour an **alias table**. That was wrong about the protocol, and the contract review caught it by RUNNING spec 17.4.0 rather than reading it. The corrected mechanism is below; ⛔ the earlier framing should not be quoted onward.

`@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0 answers an authored `dateField` on `CalendarConfigSchema` with **"Did you mean `dateField` → `endDateField`?"** — the END of the event — while every objectui read site folds that spelling onto the **start**. The divergence is real; the mechanism is **not** a contrary declaration:

- `CalendarConfigSchema`'s `strictObject` options carry `surface` and `history` and **no `aliases` entry**, so upstream declares nothing at all about either spelling. ⭐ Lit control that the option exists and is simply unused here: `GanttQuickFilterSchema`'s nested option object, in the same generated module, **does** pass `aliases: { text: 'label', … }`.
- the hint is a fallback `findClosestMatches` **Levenshtein** suggestion, budgeted `max(2, floor(len/3))`. Measured against the four known keys: `dateField` (length 9, budget 3) resolves to `endDateField` at distance 3, while `startDateField` is 5 and out of budget; `endField` (length 8, budget 2) reaches nothing, which is why it — and a nonsense control key — draw no hint at all. ⭐ Positive control that the suggester works as designed: a one-character typo of the canonical key resolves to `startDateField`.

⇒ a generic typo-distance suggester picked the wrong sibling. **Nothing upstream says `dateField` means the end of an event**, and there is no table to contradict. The hazard is author-facing all the same: someone who copies that suggestion writes `endDateField` and binds the END of an event to the date they meant as the START, which every layer accepts. Every objectui read site folds it onto the start — the retired ladder did, `normalizeListViewSchema`'s `timeline` fold does, `resolveTimelineDateBinding` documents it as "the pre-#2231 alias for `startDateField`", and this package has published "Deprecated alias for startDateField" for releases — so these arms name `startDateField` and a control pin holds that line. The remedy upstream needs is an explicit `aliases` (or `guidance`) entry for the two spellings so the suggester never answers for them; that is upstream's formatter, on upstream's card.

## Adjacency, re-derived at PR time

Twelve open pull requests enumerated through the REST API and their file lists read to the end. Exactly one overlaps: **objectui#9540** touches `packages/types/src/objectql.ts` and `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts`. Its hunks are `ObjectChartSchema` and `ObjectGallerySchema`; mine are `CalendarConfig` / `ObjectCalendarBlockConfigSchema` / `ObjectCalendarSchema` / `ListViewSchema.options`. Disjoint regions and disjoint members, so the union is "take both" with no coordination needed. objectui#9647 — named in the claim as the `packages/types` contention — touches `zod/data-display.zod.ts` and `data-display.ts` only: still no overlap. PR objectui#9471 is no longer open.

## Acceptance notes

- **Out of scope, noted, not filed:** `resolveTimelineDateBinding` in `ListView.tsx` lists `schema.calendar` / `schema.options.calendar` among its TIMELINE axis sources and folds `dateField` onto `startDateField` there. It is the timeline branch's resolver, not the calendar branch, and the timeline alias stays live by ruling — so the read is coherent today, but it is now a renderer read of a spelling the calendar block refuses. Successor: whoever takes the timeline ladder card.
- **Out of scope, noted, not filed:** the two `collectViewFields` expand-harvesters in `ListView.tsx` read `v.dateField` / `v.endField` off ANY view config. They are generic field-name collectors for `$expand`, and the timeline alias they also serve is still live, so removing the two entries would break that path. Same successor.
- ⛔ `packages/plugin-calendar/README.md` is untouched — it belongs to objectui#7925, and objectui#7925 is not addressed here.

## Contract review

`Clause-②: yes`, declared by the ruling. The card-side `needs:contract-review` carrier was hung by the dispatching seat; the PR-side carrier is hung with this pull request. The direction is a **narrowing** — two aliases become by-name refusals — so the review judges the tombstones themselves, not an accept-set growth.

Session, in prose so it survives a body rewrite: `session_012EpHzwH4wTy5sd7ibkD2yq`.
